observation.visible_scene: A clear faceted tumbler sits on a white tabletop against a smooth gray background, with a dark horizontal seam line marking the wall/table junction behind it. The glass is partly filled with several irregular ice cubes (a rounded cube near the top center, a flat cube on the left, and a cube on the right). A bright pool of reflected light and the glass's refracted shadow fall on the surface to the right of the tumbler. The composition is a close, eye-level still-life framing of the glass at left-center.
visible_changes: The ice cubes remain in the same positions and shapes throughout the excerpt; no sliding, settling, or clearly visible melting/size reduction occurs over these ~2.7 seconds.

The glass itself does not translate or rotate relative to the frame edges, and the background seam line stays at the same height, indicating an essentially fixed camera with no evident pan, tilt, or zoom.

The only perceptible variation is a subtle, non-directional flicker/shift in the brightness and soft shape of the light pool on the table to the right of the glass; this is a lighting/reflection change, not object motion.
Condensation and small water films on the glass and ice appear roughly constant, with no new droplets clearly forming within the window.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the ice melts, shrinks, or whether liquid is later poured into the glass is not shown in this segment.
The source and purpose of the bright light pool and the camera rig are not visible.
Any motion of the ice or glass before t=0 or after t=2.667 s is outside the excerpt.
uncertain_details: The small brightness changes in the right-side light pool could be sensor/lighting noise or a slight real light variation; the cause is indeterminate.
Sub-pixel differences in the glass's edge position between frames are within measurement noise, so true camera drift cannot be confirmed or ruled out.
Micro-scale melting or droplet movement, if any, is below the resolution of these sampled frames.
